summary:
The change replaces the newsletter form with a "Get early access" dialog. The dialog offers a Cal.com booking embed and a Buttondown waitlist form. It also adds GA4 marketing analytics: the control plane injects the measurement ID per deployment and the CSP is relaxed to allow the new hosts. The client-side analytics logic and its tests are solid. The change is not ready for three reasons:
- The durable run failed. All 3 control-plane failures come from a missing workspace-server build artifact (`packages/workspace-server/dist/codeExecutor.worker.js`), not from this change. Build workspace-server and rerun so the coverage for `controlPlaneHttp.ts` and `ControlPlane.ts` is recorded.
- The new CSP is broader than GA needs, and it applies to the signed-in app too.
- The new durable Playwright setup depends on Google Chrome and on a test package that `apps/web-app/package.json` does not declare.

findings.body: `webContentSecurityPolicy` is applied to every web-app response, including the signed-in workspace app served at `/`. This change adds `connect-src https://*.google.com`. That allows fetch/XHR/beacon to any google.com subdomain, for example POSTs to docs.google.com forms or script.google.com web apps, which is a ready exfiltration channel if an injection bug ever occurs. GA4 only needs `https://*.google-analytics.com` and `https://*.analytics.google.com` (plus `www.googletagmanager.com`). Replace `https://*.google.com` with `https://*.analytics.google.com`. Also note `script-src https://www.googletagmanager.com` (line 87): it allows loading any attacker-published GTM container (`gtm.js?id=GTM-…`), a known CSP bypass, for the authenticated app as well. At minimum narrow connect-src. Preferably scope the relaxed directives to the marketing responses, or add a short comment explaining why the whole app needs them. Update the control-plane test assertion to match.

The new durable E2E suite has two environment problems. (1) `channel: "chrome"` requires a system Google Chrome install. The repo provisions only Playwright Chromium: release.yml runs `playwright install chromium`, and `.agents/setup` installs Playwright Chromium. This package now joins `turbo run test:e2e` (and the release E2E gate), so on hosts without Chrome the suite fails at browser launch. Use the bundled Chromium, as `packages/extension-tools/playwright.config.ts` does, unless Chrome is truly required; if it is, install it in CI. (2) `apps/web-app/package.json` runs `playwright test` and the tests import `@playwright/test`, but the package does not declare `@playwright/test` as a devDependency. The suite resolves only through `nodeLinker: hoisted`, from whichever version Electron or extension-tools happens to hoist (1.62.1 vs ^1.61.0). Add it as a devDependency pinned to the repo's version.

testRequests.rationale: `serveWebApp` inserts the ID into HTML without escaping, so the `^G-[A-Z0-9]+$` schema pattern is the only HTML-injection guard. Add a temp test that runs `Value.Check(controlPlaneConfigSchema, …)` on both the local and cloudRun variants. It should accept `G-ABC123` and reject values such as `G-x" /><script>` and the empty string. These schema lines are currently uncovered and not exempt.

The new ControlPlane tests should cover these lines, but the durable run failed: 3 unrelated tests need the `packages/workspace-server/dist/codeExecutor.worker.js` build artifact. Build workspace-server (for example `pnpm --filter @get-halo/workspace-server build`) and rerun so the run passes and coverage is recorded.
